record.original_question: Does there exist a topological space X that satisfies the countable chain condition and is not pseudocompact, but whose Stone–Čech remainder βX − X contains no remote points, where a remote point means a point of βX − X that is not in the closure of any nowhere dense subset of X?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Is there a ccc non-pseudocompact space which has no remote points?
A remote point is a point of βX − X which is not in the closure of any nowhere dense subset of X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Tychonoff topological space, and let $\beta X$ denote its Stone–Čech compactification. A point $p\in \beta X\setminus X$ is called a remote point of $X$ if $p\notin \operatorname{cl}_{\beta X} N$ for every nowhere dense subset $N\subseteq X$. Recall that $X$ satisfies the countable chain condition (ccc) if every pairwise disjoint family of nonempty open subsets of $X$ is countable, and $X$ is pseudocompact if every continuous real-valued function on $X$ is bounded.

Question: Does there exist a Tychonoff topological space $X$ such that $X$ is ccc, $X$ is not pseudocompact, and $X$ has no remote points (i.e., $\beta X\setminus X$ contains no remote point of $X$)?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial positive results show ccc non-pseudocompact spaces have remote points in many cases: van Douwen (and independently Chae–Smith) handled countable π-weight; Dow (1984) handled π-weight ω₁; under CH, weight up to ω₂ is known to yield remote points (Brown–Dow, 2009). No ZFC example of a ccc non-pseudocompact space without remote points has been found, and the general question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Remote points under the continuum hypothesis
status_evidence.snippet: Under CH, every ccc, non-pseudocompact space of weight at most ω₂ has remote points.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (consistency) results are known; general ZFC question remains.

status_evidence.title: Remote points in large products
status_evidence.snippet: For some values of κ, ccc non-pseudocompact spaces of π-weight κ have been shown to have remote points: for κ = ω, κ = ω₁, and under CH for κ = ω₂.
status_evidence.claim: Positive results are restricted to specific π-weights or set-theoretic hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Spaces without remote points
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of non-pseudocompact spaces without remote points exist, but ccc versions remain elusive.
status_evidence.claim: No known ccc example without remote points.
